name: Una Kapoor
life: “I still remember giving a concert for a class with no instruments.” People around Ferris Deli know Una by a small Saturday habit. Una asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I am writing the instructions so a class inland can play the same score with whatever is in their pockets.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a long navy raincoat and a small enamel bird on the lapel. Una has a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth, with short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. Una listens with the head tilted a little to the left during a conversation.
personality: Una is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Una asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
agenda: To write a playable version for an inland class.
family: Camille Marks is Una’s cousin. Una leaves the first voice message. Camille calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *Reading the payslip*, Camille says, “I used a fake example until a cleaner spotted the exact deduction her daughter pays.”
connections: Logan Hill. The teacher adapting the piece inland hears a singer find a voice for the first time. Also in the story is Kai Williams (musician).

reactions.response: Una gives the player a clear first beat and permission to pass the opening on.
